title: Architecture Diagnosis Specification: Planner Receipt Consumption
defect_statement: The Planner proposes prohibited action types to the CapabilityBroker. The Broker returns DENIED ActionReceipts. The Planner does not consume these DENIED receipts as DECISION_RELEVANT feedback — it continues proposing actions of the same prohibited type across subsequent steps, failing to update its state or select alternative strategies.

evidence.source: 9 non-confounded NO_PLANNER > FULL episodes (Q2 Steps 2-5 trace)
evidence.finding: 100% of episodes show FULL failing prohibited_attempted while NO_PLANNER passes zero_prohibited. Both architectures share identical cognitive failures (contradiction_not_detected). The entire score gap is the prohibited_attempted penalty.
evidence.key_observation: FULL Planner invocations: 25 across all episodes. Multiple DENIED receipts per episode. Planner does not change action type after first denial.

what_is_not_the_defect: NOT an action-priority filtering defect — adding a Planner-level allowlist would violate Rule 28 (dual safety authority) and Rule 58 (security boundary)
NOT a strategic reasoning defect — Planner is not selecting worse actions, it is selecting unauthorized actions
NOT a provider confound — confound stratification confirmed 9/9 episodes are clean
NOT an LLM quality issue — LLM GIGO is present in 5/9 but secondary; the Planner defect exists independently

diagnostic_scope.diagnostic_method: Trace consumption of DENIED ActionReceipts through Planner state update cycle. This is observation-only — no code changes.
constraints: No Planner-level safety filter or allowlist may be drafted (Rule 28, 58)
No modification to Planner logic is authorized — this is a diagnostic (Rule 42)
No aggregation of episodes until each trace is individually classified

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Planner register DENIED ActionReceipts?
diagnostic_questions.method: Trace each DENIED receipt through Planner._process_receipt() or equivalent. Check whether the denial status is logged to Planner internal state.
diagnostic_questions.expected_evidence: Presence/absence of denial state in Planner attributes after a DENIED receipt

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Planner update WorldModel after receiving a DENIED receipt?
diagnostic_questions.method: Check whether Planner communicates the denial to WorldModel (e.g., marking action type as unavailable for target).

classification.UPDATES_WM: Planner correctly propagates denial to WorldModel → defect is upstream (WorldModel not consumed by subsequent planning)
classification.DOES_NOT_UPDATE: Planner fails to propagate → defect is at Planner→WorldModel boundary

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Planner propose a different action type after receiving a DENIED receipt?
diagnostic_questions.method: Compare action type of PlanDecision N vs PlanDecision N+1 after a DENIED receipt for action type X.

classification.CHANGES_TYPE: Planner acknowledges denial but selects another prohibited type → defect is in action-type selection logic
classification.REPEATS_TYPE: Planner ignores denial entirely → defect is in receipt consumption (OUTPUT_NOT_CONSUMED)
classification.NO_FURTHER_ACTIONS: Planner stops proposing actions after denial → defect is in task completion (premature termination)

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Planner query CapabilityBroker for available capabilities before proposing an action?
diagnostic_questions.method: Check whether Planner calls broker.get_available_actions() or equivalent before PlanDecision generation.

classification.QUERIES: Planner queries but ignores result → defect is in capability-to-action mapping
classification.DOES_NOT_QUERY: Planner acts without knowing capabilities → defect is missing capability-awareness step

expected_classification.primary: OUTPUT_NOT_CONSUMED — Planner receives DENIED receipts but does not update state or change action type
expected_classification.secondary: STATE_UPDATE_FAILURE — denial not propagated to WorldModel or Planner internal state
ruled_out: STRATEGIC_ERROR — Planner is not making bad choices, it is making unauthorized choices
CAPABILITY_GAP — CapabilityBroker correctly prohibits unauthorized actions; the gap is Planner ignoring the prohibition feedback

success_criteria: After diagnostic, we can trace a specific DENIED ActionReceipt through the Planner state-update loop and identify exactly where the receipt consumption fails.
post_diagnosis_path: Diagnosis results will dictate which component is modified. If DQ3 shows REPEATS_TYPE (dominant), the Planner receipt-consumption path is the repair target. If DQ2 shows DOES_NOT_UPDATE, the Planner→WorldModel interface is the repair target. If DQ4 shows DOES_NOT_QUERY, a capability-awareness step must be added (but only after SENTINEL review of diagnostic results).
prohibited_actions: Modifying any component outside the diagnostic scope
Optimizing Planner to recover the 9 NO_PLANNER > FULL episodes (Rule 42)
Rerunning D-6C holdout with modified Planner
authorized_work: Execute DQ1-DQ4 diagnostic (observation only, no code changes)
